newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends mildly up vs dlr in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends mildly up vs dlr in dull trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.71/72 per dollar on Monday, mildly up from the day's opening quote of 35.73/76, dealers said.

The rupee moved in the 35.69-35.74 per dollar range. The market was dampened by a strike by a section of the staff of Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which affected clearing of money market transactions, dealers said.
Premia on forward dollars rose mildly but activity in this segment too was lacklustre, dealers said.
A poll of top treasurers by Standard Chartered Bank released on Monday showed spot dollar-rupee touching a mean of 36.63 rupees per dollar in six months.
"The rupee, which was expected to weaken to a level of 35.80 by September 1 (in the August poll) dropped only to a level of 35.66 at the time of polling," Standard Chartered Bank said.
"This relative strength in the rupee is expected to remain as treasurers have polled that the rupee should reach a rate of 35.88 by October 1, 1996," a bank statement said.
